This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-4-3-1 (List and Switch Repository Branches) and REQ-1-1-2 (Sign In with an Existing Account); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes. A “branch protection rule” is a persistent merge restriction bound to one exact branch name, displayed in the frontend under Settings → Branches, with the backend storing the branch name and rule toggles. This product supports only two independently selectable requirements: “at least 1 valid Approve from someone other than the PR author” and “required check `test` is success”. For a given reviewer on the same current compare commit, only the reviewer's latest decision among Comment, Approve, and Request changes counts. The PR author cannot satisfy the approval requirement; any valid Request changes blocks merging; when the compare branch gains a new commit, all decisions become stale and a new review is required. “Checks” is the results area on the PR detail page attached to the current compare commit; the `test` status of pending, success, or failure, together with the setter and time, must be stored, and only a repository Admin may update that status from this area. The system blocks direct writes to a protected branch and applies the rule during subsequent PR merging. The repository provides a Settings link followed by a Branches link. The rule form opens from the Add branch protection rule button and contains a field labeled Branch name pattern (an exact branch name, with no wildcard semantics), checkboxes named Require 1 approval and Require status check test, and a Create button; an existing rule uses Save changes. After saving and reloading, the branch name is visible verbatim with the summaries 1 approval and Require status check test. For a non-Admin, Add branch protection rule is absent, even if Settings or Branches remain accessible; rejecting a save alone is insufficient. On the PR detail page, the Checks area is available on arrival, displays test: pending initially, and offers the Admin a combobox named test status with a clickable option named success and a Save button. Saving displays test: success and identifies the setter and time, and reloading preserves the result for that compare commit. Seed data comprises a repository Admin and a readable non-Admin account, a dedicated repository and exact branch name with no existing rule before creation, and a separate Open PR targeting protected main with its current test check initially pending.

cases.title: REQ-6-2-2: native base/compare show exact changed file and comparable commits
cases.basis: Atomic description + inherited role, scope, state and entry contracts; source review only
cases.requirement_quote:
The PR comparison page is a read-only page shown before creation: base is the target branch that receives the merge result, and compare is the source branch that provides the changes to merge. A user with Write, Maintain, Admin, or organization Owner status clicks “New pull request” on the “Pull requests” page and selects the two branches; the system calculates comparable commits, changed files, and a diff summary based on the commits they currently point to. If the branches are the same or there is no difference, the creation entry is disabled; comparison does not save a PR, commit, or branch change. This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-4-3-1 (List and Switch Repository Branches) and REQ-1-1-2 (Sign In with an Existing Account); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes. Only signed-in users with Write, Maintain, Admin, or organization Owner status may compare branches on the repository pull-request page; Read and Triage may view existing PRs but cannot enter the creation-comparison flow. The system validates the role and rejects unauthorized requests. New pull request is a link. The comparison page has native select controls with combobox roles named base and compare; each option's visible label is its exact branch name. Compare changes is a button. For a valid selection it displays the known changed file path verbatim, a Commit summary with the comparable commit count, and an enabled Create pull request button. Selecting the same branch in both fields immediately displays No changes and disables the creation button, without requiring Compare changes to be clicked first. Clicking Compare changes retains that result. Seed data supplies a contributor with Write permission, a public repository PR-list page entry, a base branch, a distinct compare branch ahead by at least one commit, and a known changed file. Separate valid comparison page entrys open the same usable creation flow with the branches already selected; these pairs have no existing Open or Draft PR at the start of each creation scenario.

The seeded changed-file path for comparison is `src/search.ts`.

Screenshot reference:
![image](reference/github-compare-branches.png)

Reloading preserves the heading and usable navigation links; leaving and reopening the same visible page restores the same PR and allows the same navigation. Seed data includes its stable title, description, discussion comment, and at least one comparable commit. Conversation is the timeline for the author's description, ordinary comments, review summaries, and status events; Commits is the list of commits on the PR's current compare branch relative to base; Files changed is the entry point to the current diff. Users with repository-view permission can switch among the three tabs; all read the same persisted PR, branch, and commit data and do not create comments, reviews, or merges. This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-6-2-3 (Create a Pull Request from Comparison Results); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes.

cases.title: REQ-6-3-2: visitor diff displays exact path and exact aggregate additions/deletions from both changed files
cases.basis: Atomic description + inherited role, scope, state and entry contracts; source review only
cases.requirement_quote: Files changed is the read-only diff view on a PR detail page computed from the current base and compare commits. From a visible public pull request entry, a visitor activates the Files changed link and sees the known changed file path verbatim and visible aggregate text such as 3 additions, 1 deletions. cases.title: REQ-6-3-3: single inline comment persists at changed line
cases.basis: Atomic description + inherited role, scope, state and entry contracts; source review only
cases.requirement_quote: An inline review comment is a comment record anchored to a file path, the current compare commit, and a specific added/deleted line in Files changed; it differs from an ordinary comment in Conversation that has no code location. A user with Write, Maintain, or Admin who is not the PR author can hover over a changed line, click the button visually shown as “+” and accessibly named Add comment, and choose “Add single comment” to publish immediately or “Start a review” to keep it as a pending review draft. The changed-line Add comment buttons are available for direct activation without a prerequisite hover; the first such button in document order targets the first commentable changed line. Activating one opens a single editor labeled Comment with Add single comment and Start a review buttons. Add single comment immediately displays the exact entered body in that diff view and retains it after reload. Start a review displays the body and Pending review to its author immediately, retains the pending draft after reload, and does not make it public before review submission. Seed data supplies a non-author Write reviewer, an Open reviewable PR with at least one changed line, and a separate Open PR for the pending-comment scenario. The system stores the PR, file path, compare commit, line position, author, body, and publication state; when the compare commit changes, published comments are retained but marked Outdated, while drafts are not published automatically. This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-6-3-2 (Inspect Changed Files and Aggregate Diff) and REQ-1-1-2 (Sign In with an Existing Account); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes.

cases.title: REQ-6-3-4: Approve submission persists current-commit review
cases.basis: Atomic description + inherited role, scope, state and entry contracts; source review only
cases.requirement_quote: From the Files changed link, the reviewer activates the Review changes button to open one review form with an optional Summary field, radio controls named Comment, Approve, and Request changes, and a Submit review button. Selecting Approve and submitting without a summary is valid and displays Approved. Selecting Request changes with a summary displays Changes requested and that exact summary; the decision remains visible after reload. Seed data supplies a non-author Write reviewer and separate Open PRs for approval and request-changes submission, with no initial effective decision by that reviewer. A user who is not the PR author and has Write, Maintain, or Admin may submit Comment, Approve, or Request changes on an Open PR; the author and Draft PRs cannot submit reviews. The system stores the review decision, reviewer, current compare commit, optional explanation, and time; a new decision by the same reviewer replaces that reviewer's effective decision for the current commit while preserving the old record. Approve is valid only when the reviewer is not the author and the compare commit is still the same; Request changes blocks merging until that reviewer submits a new Comment or Approve for the current compare commit, or the compare branch receives a new commit that makes the old decision stale. This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-6-3-1 (View Pull Request Overview and Commits) and REQ-1-1-2 (Sign In with an Existing Account); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes.

cases.title: REQ-6-4: author requests and removes live eligible reviewer without confirmation
cases.basis: Atomic description + inherited role, scope, state and entry contracts; source review only
cases.requirement_quote: The Reviewers button opens a picker with a textbox named Search. Typing an eligible username immediately reveals an option with that exact accessible name. Selecting the option saves the request immediately without a separate Save action, closes the picker, and displays the username in the reviewer area; it remains after reload. Each requested reviewer has a button named Remove followed by a space and the username; clicking it immediately removes the request and the username from that area, without a confirmation step. The seed PR is Open, belongs to the signed-in author, and initially has no request or submitted review from the eligible target reviewer; the target is a distinct non-author collaborator with Write or higher permission. Removing a request persists across reload. A “reviewer request” is a pending-review relationship between a PR and a candidate reviewer account, displayed in the Reviewers area on the right side of the PR detail page; it is not the same as a submitted review decision. The author of an Open or Draft PR, Maintain, Admin, or organization Owner may create or delete this relationship. Matching reviewer options update as the user types in the search textbox; pressing Enter or activating a separate search button is not required before selecting an option. A candidate reviewer must have Write, Maintain, or Admin on the repository and must not be the PR author; the system stores or deletes the “PR-reviewer request” relationship together with the operator and time. Removing a request does not delete reviews, comments, or activity records already submitted by that user and does not change the user's effective review decision. This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-6-2-3 (Create a Pull Request from Comparison Results) and REQ-1-1-2 (Sign In with an Existing Account); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes.

cases.title: REQ-6-5: Maintain merge commits actual changes to base branch and persists terminal status
cases.basis: Atomic description + inherited role, scope, state and entry contracts; source review only
cases.requirement_quote: On an eligible PR, Merge pull request and then Confirm merge are buttons; confirming displays Merged, and that state remains after reload. A blocked PR keeps a visible disabled Merge pull request button and explains its unmet review or protection condition before any click. Seed data supplies a Maintain account and separate Open PRs for success and refusal. The eligible PR targets protected main, has a current non-author approval and test: success, and has no conflicts. The blocked PR targets a protected branch and lacks the required valid approval; its disabled button is accompanied by Review required by branch protection. Each seed state is restored independently before reuse. “Merge” is the only write operation that writes the current compare commit's changes from an Open PR into the base branch; it is not simply marking the PR as complete. Only Maintain, Admin, or organization Owner may merge from the PR detail page using the sole supported “Create a merge commit” method; the merge confirmation area should display satisfied and unsatisfied conditions. Before confirmation, the system rereads the target branch head, current compare commit, merge-conflict state, and protection rules — there must be no valid Request changes; if the target is protected, each enabled rule requirement is enforced independently, requiring 1 valid non-author Approve for the current compare commit when Require 1 approval is enabled and requiring `test` success when Require status check test is enabled. An unprotected target has no additional approval-count or check-success requirement, but merging still requires no merge conflicts and no valid Request changes review. After validation succeeds, the system atomically creates a merge commit whose parents are the target-branch head at merge time and the current compare commit, updates the target-branch head, sets the PR to Merged, and stores the merger, time, and resulting commit identifier. If any condition is unsatisfied or persistence fails, the page explains the applicable reason and neither the target branch nor PR changes; a missing required approval displays “Review required by branch protection”. Merged is terminal. This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-6-3-4 (Submit a Pull Request Review) and REQ-6-1 (Protect Branches with Review and Status-Check Requirements); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes.

requirement_quotes.REQ-1-1-2:
This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-1-1-1 (Register a New GitHub Account); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes. The sign-in page is the form on the account-access page containing “Username or email”, “Password”, and “Sign in”. A “session” is the current-browser login record saved after successful account authentication, represented in the frontend by the upper-right account menu and access to protected pages. The visitor enters a username or email and a password and submits the form. The system looks up the account and validates its credentials and availability status; if authentication fails due to an unknown username/email, incorrect password, or unavailable account, the system displays exactly the same generic failure message “Invalid credentials”, does not disclose whether the account exists or which credential was wrong, and does not create a session. After successful authentication, the system stores a session with a unique session identifier, account identifier, and active status, then redirects to the workspace accessible to that user; the session remains valid after refreshing or reopening the workspace, and subsequent protected organization, repository, and work-item requests must use this session to determine the current user.

Screenshot reference:
![image](reference/github-sign-in.png)
requirement_quotes.REQ-4-2-1:
This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-4-1 (Browse Repository Files and Directories); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes. Any user with repository-view permission can read branch history on the Commits page, or from a file page read only the history that modified that file; each record references the stored commit identifier, author, time, message, parent commit, and changed files. The repository and file pages each expose one history link named “Commits” (a commit count may accompany the visible label without introducing another matching link). Seed history includes a known commit message and author, displayed in full as distinct readable text values, and a relative timestamp containing “ago”. Opening the branch history directly from the repository must show these values without first selecting a file-specific scope.

Screenshot reference:
![image](reference/github-commit-history.png)
requirement_quotes.REQ-4-2-2:
This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-4-2-1 (View Repository Commit History); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes. Any user with repository-view permission can compare two readable commits or revisions on the diff page; the page reads and displays the changed files and line-by-line additions and deletions between them without creating a review, comment, or commit. A seeded commit has an accessible commit entry, a known changed-file path `src/search.ts`, and a readable parent revision. Opening that commit entry as a visitor displays the changed-file path as an exact text value, the “Changed files” summary, and the numeric additions/deletions summary described below, without requiring previous navigation through history.

Screenshot reference:
![image](reference/github-commit-diff.png)
requirement_quotes.REQ-4-4:
This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-4-1 (Browse Repository Files and Directories) and REQ-1-1-2 (Sign In with an Existing Account); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes. The file editor is the form opened from Edit or Add file on the Code page; the user edits file content at a path on the current branch and submits it. Only Write, Maintain, Admin, or organization Owner may submit; Read and Triage may only view. A single submission stores the file-path and content change, commit message, author, parent commit, and target branch as one indivisible record and moves the target branch to point to that new commit. A new or renamed file path must not be empty, must not begin with `/`, must not contain a `..` path segment, and must not conflict with an existing file or directory on the current branch; the commit message must contain 1–72 non-empty characters after trimming leading and trailing whitespace. If the path conflicts, content validation fails, the commit message is noncompliant, the branch is protected, or persistence fails, the page displays the reason and does not change the file, branch head, or commit history. An invalid path displays “Invalid file path”, and an empty commit message displays “Commit message is required”. From the writable Code page, the unique “Add file” button opens the “Create new file” menuitem. The editor has a field labeled “File name”, a textbox named “File contents”, an initially empty field labeled “Commit message”, and a “Commit changes” button. Creating a unique file such as `pw-file-<unique suffix>.md` with nonempty text and a message such as `Add <file name>` immediately opens a view displaying the exact saved content. Its “Commits” link opens history displaying the exact submitted message. Submitting `../invalid.md` with content `must not be saved` and no commit message reports the invalid path and/or required message and changes neither files nor history. The example content is ordinary text, not a forbidden content value by itself; rejection follows from the invalid path or missing message.

This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-1-1-1 (Register a New GitHub Account); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes. requirement_quotes.REQ-4-2-1:

requirement_quotes.REQ-4-2-2:

requirement_quotes.REQ-4-4:
This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-4-1 (Browse Repository Files and Directories) and REQ-1-1-2 (Sign In with an Existing Account); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes. The file editor is the form opened from Edit or Add file on the Code page; the user edits file content at a path on the current branch and submits it. Only Write, Maintain, Admin, or organization Owner may submit; Read and Triage may only view. A single submission stores the file-path and content change, commit message, author, parent commit, and target branch as one indivisible record and moves the target branch to point to that new commit. A new or renamed file path must not be empty, must not begin with `/`, must not contain a `..` path segment, and must not conflict with an existing file or directory on the current branch; the commit message must contain 1–72 non-empty characters after trimming leading and trailing whitespace. If the path conflicts, content validation fails, the commit message is noncompliant, the branch is protected, or persistence fails, the page displays the reason and does not change the file, branch head, or commit history. An invalid path displays “Invalid file path”, and an empty commit message displays “Commit message is required”. From the writable Code page, the unique “Add file” button opens the “Create new file” menuitem. The editor has a field labeled “File name”, a textbox named “File contents”, an initially empty field labeled “Commit message”, and a “Commit changes” button. Creating a unique file such as `pw-file-<unique suffix>.md` with nonempty text and a message such as `Add <file name>` immediately opens a view displaying the exact saved content. Its “Commits” link opens history displaying the exact submitted message. Submitting `../invalid.md` with content `must not be saved` and no commit message reports the invalid path and/or required message and changes neither files nor history. The example content is ordinary text, not a forbidden content value by itself; rejection follows from the invalid path or missing message.

![image](reference/github-web-file-editor.png)

cases.title: INTEGRATION-team-access: guide: direct team grant changes effective permissions without hierarchy inheritance or account deletion
cases.basis: Atomic description + inherited role, scope, state and entry contracts; source review only
cases.requirement_quote: From the repository's “Settings” link, open the “Manage access” link and activate “Add people or teams”. The picker presents a textbox “Search”, a matching selectable team option whose name contains the team name, a combobox “Role” with clickable role options including “Write”, and an “Add” button. While the picker is active, hide the opening Add people or teams button from the active view so the submit action is unambiguous. After saving, the authorization list visibly shows the exact team name and Write role and retains the team after reload. Existing grants appear as rows whose accessible names include the subject name; each row contains a native select labeled “Role” and a “Save” button. Selecting the option labeled “Read” and saving replaces Write; after reload exactly one row for the team remains and contains Read. The creation scenario supplies a repository Admin and an organization team not yet granted access; the replacement scenario supplies a separate repository/team with an existing Write grant. An organization Owner or repository Admin may grant a repository role of Read, Triage, Write, Maintain, or Admin to a current organization member or team. In the access-subject picker, matching member or team options update as the administrator types; pressing Enter or activating a separate search button is not required before selecting an option. A private repository is accessible only to an organization Owner, a member with a direct repository role, or a direct member of a team that has a repository role; an ordinary organization Member has no default private-repository access. For a given subject and repository, only one direct role grant is stored — saving the same role again does not create a second record, and changing the role replaces the original role. An account's effective repository role is the highest among Admin from Owner status and all still-valid direct grants and team grants; team hierarchy does not propagate membership or authorization. The system stores the authorization subject, repository, role, grantor, and timestamp and authorizes operations according to the ROOT role matrix; unauthorized accounts cannot see private repositories. This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-2-1-2 (Create an Organization After Authentication) and REQ-2-2-1 (Create an Organization Team); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes.

requirement_quotes.REQ-2-2-2: Only an organization Owner may maintain members or hierarchy on an organization team page. The team maintainer in these scenarios is an organization Owner. After adding, the member's complete username is visible once in the member list, alongside a button named “Remove <username>”. Activating this removal button immediately removes that member without a second confirmation step, and reload keeps the username absent. Settings contains a native select with combobox role labeled “Parent team”, whose option labels are team names, and a button “Save”. The original parent remains selected after a rejected change and reload. The cycle scenario supplies a team with an existing parent and a descendant selectable by name; submitting that descendant shows the cycle error rather than saving it. The seed record's original-parent value identifies the stored selection, which may differ from its display label. The membership scenario supplies a current organization member not yet in this team. On the team page, the Owner clicks “Members” to add or remove current organization members, or selects a new parent team in “Settings” and saves. The system stores the team-membership relationship or team hierarchy and immediately reflects it in the organization team tree and member list; team hierarchy creates no implicit membership relationship or repository permission, and cyclic hierarchy is prohibited. A rejected cycle displays “Cyclic team hierarchy is not allowed”. This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-2-2-1 (Create an Organization Team); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes.
requirement_quotes.REQ-2-3: From the repository's “Settings” link, open the “Manage access” link and activate “Add people or teams”. The picker presents a textbox “Search”, a matching selectable team option whose name contains the team name, a combobox “Role” with clickable role options including “Write”, and an “Add” button. While the picker is active, hide the opening Add people or teams button from the active view so the submit action is unambiguous. After saving, the authorization list visibly shows the exact team name and Write role and retains the team after reload. Existing grants appear as rows whose accessible names include the subject name; each row contains a native select labeled “Role” and a “Save” button. Selecting the option labeled “Read” and saving replaces Write; after reload exactly one row for the team remains and contains Read. The creation scenario supplies a repository Admin and an organization team not yet granted access; the replacement scenario supplies a separate repository/team with an existing Write grant. An organization Owner or repository Admin may grant a repository role of Read, Triage, Write, Maintain, or Admin to a current organization member or team. In the access-subject picker, matching member or team options update as the administrator types; pressing Enter or activating a separate search button is not required before selecting an option. A private repository is accessible only to an organization Owner, a member with a direct repository role, or a direct member of a team that has a repository role; an ordinary organization Member has no default private-repository access. For a given subject and repository, only one direct role grant is stored — saving the same role again does not create a second record, and changing the role replaces the original role. An account's effective repository role is the highest among Admin from Owner status and all still-valid direct grants and team grants; team hierarchy does not propagate membership or authorization. The system stores the authorization subject, repository, role, grantor, and timestamp and authorizes operations according to the ROOT role matrix; unauthorized accounts cannot see private repositories. This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-2-1-2 (Create an Organization After Authentication) and REQ-2-2-1 (Create an Organization Team); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes.

Open the repository's “Settings” link and then its “General” link to reach Danger Zone. The visibility action is a button “Change visibility”; the confirmation flow provides a “Public” radio and a button “Confirm visibility”. Selecting Public and activating Confirm visibility completes the change without requiring the repository name to be retyped or any additional mandatory field. A non-Admin collaborator must not see the Change visibility button, including when a Settings link is available. Seed data supplies an Admin, a distinct non-Admin collaborator, and a currently private repository containing public-ready content. After successful confirmation, a visible Public marker appears, and an unauthenticated visitor reopening the same address sees its repository heading. A repository administrator changes repository visibility after reviewing the impact on access permissions. The system blocks unauthorized changes, applies the selected visibility, and enforces the updated access rules when users subsequently open the repository.

requirement_quotes.REQ-4-4:
This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-4-1 (Browse Repository Files and Directories) and REQ-1-1-2 (Sign In with an Existing Account); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes. The file editor is the form opened from Edit or Add file on the Code page; the user edits file content at a path on the current branch and submits it. Only Write, Maintain, Admin, or organization Owner may submit; Read and Triage may only view. A single submission stores the file-path and content change, commit message, author, parent commit, and target branch as one indivisible record and moves the target branch to point to that new commit. A new or renamed file path must not be empty, must not begin with `/`, must not contain a `..` path segment, and must not conflict with an existing file or directory on the current branch; the commit message must contain 1–72 non-empty characters after trimming leading and trailing whitespace. If the path conflicts, content validation fails, the commit message is noncompliant, the branch is protected, or persistence fails, the page displays the reason and does not change the file, branch head, or commit history. An invalid path displays “Invalid file path”, and an empty commit message displays “Commit message is required”. From the writable Code page, the unique “Add file” button opens the “Create new file” menuitem. The editor has a field labeled “File name”, a textbox named “File contents”, an initially empty field labeled “Commit message”, and a “Commit changes” button. Creating a unique file such as `pw-file-<unique suffix>.md` with nonempty text and a message such as `Add <file name>` immediately opens a view displaying the exact saved content. Its “Commits” link opens history displaying the exact submitted message. Submitting `../invalid.md` with content `must not be saved` and no commit message reports the invalid path and/or required message and changes neither files nor history. The example content is ordinary text, not a forbidden content value by itself; rejection follows from the invalid path or missing message.
